fit_reason: Snowflake runs the Data Cloud that unifies scattered enterprise data into one governed foundation for analytics, applications and data sharing, which makes it a vendor that makes data usable and an incumbent data platform adapting for agents. Usable data is what is scarce because most enterprise data is not agent ready, and cleanup and retrieval demand grows as companies deploy agents. Data is the whole business, and it is one of the leading independent cloud data platforms.

S&P Global sells ratings, benchmarks, indices, market intelligence and commodity and automotive data, making it a data provider whose datasets are proprietary and hard to replicate. Hard-to-replicate data holds its value whichever models win, and holders can license it or build AI products and APIs on it. Data is central to every segment, and it is one of the largest financial data franchises in the world.

RELX runs LexisNexis Risk, Elsevier scientific content and LexisNexis legal, so it is a data provider with deep proprietary and domain-specific datasets in risk, science and law. Domain-specific content and accumulated judgment are the hardest data to reproduce, and RELX is already building AI legal and research tools on it. Data and analytics are central to the business, and it is a global leader in professional information.

MongoDB sells a document database and the Atlas managed service with built-in vector search, making it a database vendor making its database usable by agents. Agents that carry context across sessions need it stored and retrieved, which adds demand for databases built for retrieval. The database is the whole business, and it is the leading independent document database.

Palantir's Foundry and AIP platforms integrate an organization's structured and unstructured data into an ontology that LLMs and agents can act on, so it is a vendor that cleans, organizes and structures messy enterprise data. Most enterprise data is not agent ready, and vendors that make it usable gain as companies try to deploy agents. Making data usable is central to its business, and it is one of the most prominent enterprise AI data platforms.

Thomson Reuters holds Westlaw legal content, tax and accounting research and Reuters news, making it a data provider with proprietary domain content that it is building AI assistants on. Domain-specific content is hard to replicate and holds its value whichever models win, and holders can build applications on it. Content and data are central to the business, and it is a leading legal and tax information provider.

Verisk supplies insurance data and analytics built on industry-contributed policy and claims records, which makes it a data provider with a proprietary dataset that insurers depend on. Data that is hard to replicate is the most valuable and safest, and Verisk can build models and applications for underwriting and claims on it. Data analytics is the whole business, and it is the dominant data provider to US property and casualty insurers.

MSCI licenses indexes, risk analytics, ESG ratings and private asset data, making it a data provider with proprietary benchmarks and datasets. Proprietary data holds its value whichever models win, and MSCI can license it or offer it through APIs to agents. Data and analytics are central to the business, and it is a leading index and risk analytics provider.

Moody's issues credit ratings and sells research, credit data and analytics through Moody's Analytics, making it a data provider with proprietary credit information. Hard-to-replicate data is the most valuable for building task-specific models and applications, which Moody's is doing with its analytics products. Ratings and data are central to the business, and it is one of the two dominant credit rating agencies.

London Stock Exchange Group sells financial data, analytics, pricing and FTSE Russell indexes through its Data and Analytics business, making it a data provider. Proprietary market data can be licensed or offered through APIs to agents and model builders, which is where holders gain. Data and analytics is its largest segment, and it is one of the largest financial data providers globally.

Meta operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, generating proprietary data about billions of users and their activity, which makes it a platform that holds data as a byproduct of operating. Holders with proprietary data and users can build models and applications on it, and Meta trains its own models on its platform data. Its business is built on this data, and it is one of the largest data holders in the world.

Alphabet runs Search, YouTube, Maps and Android, generating proprietary data on queries, video and location, and builds its own models on it while also selling database and analytics services in Google Cloud. Platforms with proprietary data can build models and applications on it, which is where the value ends up. Data is central to its advertising business, and it is one of the largest data holders and model builders.

Tyler Technologies runs courts, tax, records, public safety and financial systems for state and local governments, so it is a vertical software company that holds data as a byproduct of the work that runs inside its systems. Vertical software data is more structured and closer to agent ready, and holders can build domain-specific applications on it. Public sector software is its whole business, and it is the largest US public sector software provider.

Veeva provides CRM, content management and clinical software plus data products such as OpenData, Link and Crossix for life sciences, making it vertical software that also sells data. Vertical data is structured and hard to replicate, and Veeva can build domain-specific AI applications on it. Life sciences software and data is its whole business, and it is the leading software provider to the pharmaceutical industry.

IQVIA supplies real-world healthcare data, prescription data and analytics alongside clinical research services, making it a data provider. Real-world healthcare data is proprietary and hard to replicate, and IQVIA can build domain-specific models and applications for life sciences on it. Data and analytics are central to its Technology and Analytics segment, and it is the largest healthcare data provider to pharma.

Equifax holds consumer credit data and The Work Number employment and income records, making it a data provider with proprietary datasets. Hard-to-replicate data is the safest and most valuable, and Equifax can license it and build decisioning products on it. Data and analytics is the whole business, and it is one of the three major US credit bureaus.

TransUnion holds consumer credit, identity and fraud data, making it a data provider whose records cannot be easily replicated. Proprietary data holds its value whichever models win, and TransUnion can offer it through APIs and build analytics on it. Data is the whole business, and it is one of the three major US credit bureaus.

FactSet provides integrated financial data and analytics to investment professionals, making it a data provider. Holders of proprietary data can offer it to agents through APIs and build AI workflows on it, though some of its content is aggregated rather than original. Data is the whole business, and it is a leading financial data provider to asset managers and banks.

Elastic sells Elasticsearch, a search and analytics engine with vector search that stores and retrieves structured and unstructured data, making it a retrieval-oriented database vendor. Persistent agent memory and retrieval-augmented generation add demand for databases built for retrieval. Search and retrieval is the whole business, and Elasticsearch is one of the most widely used search engines.

Tempus AI runs genomic diagnostics and holds a large library of linked de-identified clinical, molecular and imaging data that it licenses and builds AI on, making it a data provider. Multimodal clinical data is hard to replicate, and holders can license it or build models on it. Data is central to its strategy, and it is one of the largest holders of linked oncology data.

Innodata provides data engineering for AI, including data annotation, curation, transformation and training data for model builders, making it both a company building data deliberately for labs and a vendor that cleans and structures data. Usable data is scarce, and companies that supply training data to labs gain as models are built and fine-tuned. Data engineering is its whole business, though it is a small player next to private data suppliers.

Guidewire runs policy, billing and claims core systems for property and casualty insurers, plus data and analytics tools, making it a vertical software company holding insurance data. Vertical software data is structured and close to agent ready, and Guidewire can build insurance-specific AI on it. Insurance core software is its whole business, and it is the leading P and C core system vendor.

CCC Intelligent Solutions runs a SaaS network connecting auto insurers, repairers and parts suppliers and processes claims and estimates with AI, making it a vertical software company holding a large claims dataset. Accumulated domain data is hard to replicate and supports AI products such as its estimating tools. Insurance claims software is its whole business, and it is the dominant auto claims platform in the US.

Teradata provides the Vantage data platform for enterprise analytics across clouds, making it an incumbent data platform vendor adapting for AI. Enterprise data that is not agent ready creates demand for platforms that unify and organize it, though newer platforms compete hard. Data platforms are its whole business, but it is a mature player losing ground to cloud-native rivals.

Morningstar sells investment data, research, ratings, indexes and PitchBook private market data, making it a data provider. Proprietary research and private market data are hard to replicate and can be licensed or built into AI tools. Data and research are the whole business, and it is a leading independent investment data provider.

Reddit hosts community discussions that form a large proprietary corpus of human conversation, and it licenses this data to AI model builders, making it a platform that holds data as a byproduct. Its data is one of the few large sources of fresh human discussion that labs want, and licensing is a direct route for holders to gain. Data is central to its business, and it is a notable supplier of training data to major labs.

AppLovin runs ad-tech that matches advertisers with mobile app inventory, generating proprietary data on user engagement and conversion that its AI models use, making it a platform named in the sub-sector. Platforms that generate proprietary data can build models on it, and AppLovin's ad engine is built on its own data. Data-driven advertising is the whole business, and it is a leading mobile advertising platform.

NIQ analyzes retail and consumer shopping data to provide consumer insights to brands and retailers, making it a data provider. Proprietary retail measurement data is hard to replicate and can be licensed or built into AI tools. Data is the whole business, and it is the largest retail measurement provider globally.

Oracle sells the Oracle Database, MySQL HeatWave and Fusion ERP, so it is a database vendor adapting its databases for agents and a system of record holding enterprise data. Retrieval demand from agents and enterprise data held in its systems both add demand, though much of its current growth is cloud infrastructure. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the largest enterprise database vendor.

Microsoft sells SQL Server, Fabric and Azure data services and owns LinkedIn and Bing, making it both a database vendor and a platform with proprietary data. Retrieval and data platforms gain as agents are adopted, and LinkedIn holds hard-to-replicate professional data. Data is a meaningful part of a broader business, and it is one of the largest data platform vendors.

Samsara collects data from its own IoT devices on fleets and physical operations into a data platform with AI and analytics, making it a platform that generates proprietary sensor and telematics data. Hard-to-replicate operational data supports AI safety and operations products built on it. Its business is built on this data, and it is a leading connected operations platform.

Procore runs construction management software for owners and contractors, holding project, financial and document data as a byproduct, making it a vertical software company. Vertical software data is structured and closer to agent ready, and Procore can build construction-specific AI on it. Construction software is its whole business, and it is the leading construction management platform.

AppFolio provides property management software that acts as the system of record for property managers, making it a vertical software company holding real estate operating data. Structured vertical data supports AI applications, and AppFolio is building AI into leasing and maintenance workflows. Property management software is its whole business, and it is a leading platform for small and mid-sized property managers.

Toast runs POS, payments and back-office software for restaurants, holding transaction and operating data as a byproduct, making it a vertical software company. Vertical software data is structured and supports domain-specific AI, though transaction records are easier to replicate than accumulated judgment. Restaurant software is its whole business, and it is a leading restaurant platform in the US.

Intuit runs QuickBooks, TurboTax, Credit Karma and Mailchimp, holding financial data for millions of small businesses and consumers, making it a holder of proprietary data where financial work runs. Holders with proprietary data and customers can build agents and applications on it, which Intuit is doing. Its products are built on this data, and it is the leading small business and consumer tax software provider.

SAP's S/4HANA ERP, SuccessFactors and Business Network hold core financial, supply chain and HR data for large enterprises, and its Business Data Cloud organizes it for AI, making it a system of record that holds data. Enterprise data in ERP is structured, and SAP can build agents on it, though the data belongs to customers. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the largest ERP vendor.

Salesforce holds customer data in its CRM and sells Data Cloud, Tableau and MuleSoft to unify and connect enterprise data, making it a holder of customer data and a vendor making data usable. Unified, agent-ready customer data is what agents need, and Salesforce is building its agent products on it. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the largest CRM vendor.

OpenText sells information management software for enterprise content, documents and data, with AI and analytics for structured and unstructured data, making it a vendor that organizes messy enterprise data. Most enterprise content is unstructured and not agent ready, which creates demand for vendors that organize it. Information management is central to the business, and it is a large incumbent in enterprise content management.

Box provides cloud content management for enterprise files with AI built on top, making it a vendor that organizes and makes unstructured enterprise content usable by agents. Unstructured content is much of what enterprises hold, and making it agent ready adds demand. Content management is its whole business, and it is a leading independent enterprise content platform.

Clarivate provides structured data and analytics such as Web of Science, Derwent patents and Cortellis life sciences intelligence, making it a data provider. Scientific and IP data is domain-specific and hard to replicate, and it can be licensed or built into AI research tools. Information services are its whole business, though it has struggled to grow.

Wiley publishes scientific, technical and medical journals and learning content, making it a holder of proprietary domain content that it licenses, including to AI developers. Domain-specific content is hard to replicate, and licensing it to model builders is a direct route for holders to gain. Content is its whole business, and it is a major scholarly publisher.

Agilysys provides property management, POS and inventory software for hospitality, named in the sub-sector as a vertical software company holding data. Vertical software data is structured and closer to agent ready, supporting hospitality-specific AI. Hospitality software is its whole business, though it is a smaller player.

Intapp provides cloud software for law, accounting, consulting and private capital firms with an industry-specific data architecture, making it a vertical software company. Relationship and engagement data from professional firms is domain-specific and supports AI applications built on it. Vertical software is its whole business, and it is a leading provider to professional services firms.

ServiceTitan runs field service management software for residential and commercial trades, holding job, pricing and customer data, making it a vertical software company. Vertical data is structured and supports trade-specific AI applications. Field service software is its whole business, and it is the leading platform for the trades.

Descartes provides logistics and supply chain software plus global trade data intelligence, making it a vertical software company and data provider. Its logistics network and trade data are hard to replicate and support AI applications. Logistics software and data are its whole business, and it is a leading logistics network operator.

AvePoint provides data management and governance software that makes collaboration data AI ready, making it a vendor that cleans, organizes and governs enterprise data. Messy enterprise data creates demand for vendors that make it usable for agents. Data management is its whole business, though it is a small player.

Sportradar collects and distributes official sports data and odds to betting operators and media, making it a data provider with exclusive league data rights. Exclusive data rights are hard to replicate and support AI-driven products. Sports data is its whole business, and it is one of the two leading sports data providers.

Genius Sports collects and distributes official live sports data and odds feeds under league partnerships, making it a data provider. Exclusive league data is hard to replicate and can be licensed or built into products. Sports data is its whole business, and it holds key league rights such as the NFL.

Zeta Global runs a marketing platform built on a large opted-in consumer dataset and a customer data platform, making it a data provider and a platform that unifies customer data. Proprietary consumer data supports AI-driven marketing, though consumer intent data is easier to replicate than domain judgment. Data is central to the business, and it is a mid-sized marketing data player.

Red Violet provides identity intelligence built on its proprietary data fusion of public and commercial records, making it a data provider. Identity data holds value for fraud and verification use cases, though similar data is available from larger rivals. Data is its whole business, but it is a small player.

PDF Solutions provides the Exensio analytics platform that centralizes semiconductor manufacturing, test and assembly data, making it a vertical software company holding and organizing domain data. Manufacturing data is domain-specific and hard to replicate, supporting AI for yield and process control. It is central to the business, and it is a niche leader in semiconductor analytics.

Blackbaud provides fundraising, financial and student information software for nonprofits and schools, holding donor and institutional data, making it a vertical software company. Vertical data is structured and supports sector-specific AI. Nonprofit software is its whole business, and it is the leading nonprofit software provider.

Yelp hosts local business reviews and data and licenses it through the Yelp Fusion API and content licensing, making it a platform with proprietary data. Licensing and API access are direct routes for holders to gain from agents. Its business is built on this content, though it is a mid-sized platform.

Planet Labs operates satellite constellations that collect daily global imagery, making it a data provider of proprietary geospatial data. Daily global imagery is hard to replicate and supports AI analytics for government and commercial customers. Data is its whole business, and it operates the largest Earth imaging constellation.

Gartner sells subscription research, benchmarks and expert access to IT and business leaders, making it a data provider of proprietary research. Its research and benchmarks are domain-specific, though AI may make some generic advice easier to replicate. Research is its whole business, and it is the leading IT research firm.

Amplitude provides behavioral analytics built on its proprietary Behavioral Graph database and data management tools, making it a vendor that organizes customer behavior data. Usable behavioral data supports AI-driven personalization, but the data belongs to customers. Analytics is its whole business, though it is a small player.

Workday runs HR and financial systems of record for large enterprises, holding workforce and financial data, making it a holder of data where work runs. Structured HR and financial data supports agents built on it. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading HCM vendor.

ServiceNow runs IT, HR and customer service workflows with a configuration management database, holding enterprise workflow data. Workflow and configuration data supports agents, though its main role is as a system where work runs. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading enterprise workflow platform.

Intercontinental Exchange runs exchanges, fixed income data services and mortgage technology, making it a data provider alongside its marketplaces. Proprietary pricing and mortgage data are hard to replicate and can be licensed. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a major exchange and data operator.

Amazon runs a retail marketplace that generates proprietary shopping data and AWS, which sells database, analytics and data services, making it a platform holding data and a database vendor. Platform data and retrieval services both gain from agent adoption. Data is a meaningful part of a broad business, and it is one of the largest platforms and clouds.

IBM sells data and AI software, integration and databases, plus consulting on data and analytics, making it a vendor that makes enterprise data usable. Messy enterprise data creates demand for data integration and governance tools. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a large incumbent.

Accenture provides data management, data governance and AI consulting that helps enterprises clean, organize and structure their data, making it a vendor that makes messy enterprise data usable. Most enterprise data is not agent ready, so cleanup work grows as companies try to deploy agents. Data and AI services are a meaningful part of a broad consulting business, and it is the largest IT consultancy in the world.

Adobe holds licensed creative content through Adobe Stock and trains its own Firefly models on it, and its Experience Cloud includes a customer data platform, making it a holder of proprietary content and customer data. Holders that build models and applications on content they control gain as AI is adopted. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading creative software vendor.

ADP runs payroll and HR for a large share of US employers, holding proprietary employment and payroll data. Payroll data is hard to replicate and supports analytics and AI built on it. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the largest payroll provider.

Nasdaq distributes market data, licenses indexes and sells financial crime software alongside its exchanges, making it a data provider. Market data and index licensing are proprietary. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a major exchange operator.

CME Group runs futures exchanges and sells real-time and historical market data, making it a data provider alongside its marketplace. Exclusive market data is hard to replicate. Data is a meaningful but secondary part of the business, and it is the largest derivatives exchange.

FICO provides credit scores and decisioning software built on analytics of credit data, making it a holder of proprietary scoring models and data management tools. Proprietary scores are embedded in lending decisions and hard to replicate. Data and analytics are meaningful, and it is the dominant credit scoring provider.

Mastercard runs a global payment network and sells proprietary insights from transaction data, making it a network that generates data as a byproduct. Transaction data is valuable but easier to replicate than domain judgment. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is one of two global card networks.

Visa runs VisaNet, generating transaction data as a byproduct of processing payments, making it a payment network that holds data. Transaction data supports value-added services, though it is less unique than domain data. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the largest card network.

American Express runs a closed-loop card network that sees both the cardholder and the merchant side of each transaction, generating proprietary spending data as a byproduct. Transaction data supports AI for fraud, credit and merchant services, though it is easier to replicate than domain judgment. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a major card issuer and network.

Tencent operates WeChat, games, ads and cloud, generating proprietary user data and building its own models on it, making it a platform holding data. Platform data supports model and application building. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is one of the largest platforms in China.

Alibaba operates Taobao, Tmall and Alibaba Cloud and builds its own Qwen models, making it a platform holding commerce data and a cloud database vendor. Platform data and cloud data services both gain from agent adoption. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading Chinese platform.

MercadoLibre runs a marketplace, Mercado Pago payments and an ads business in Latin America, generating proprietary commerce and financial data as a byproduct, making it a platform holding data. Platforms with proprietary data can build models and applications on it, such as credit and ads. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading Latin American e-commerce and fintech platform.

Shopify runs the commerce platform for millions of merchants, holding product catalog, order and shopper data as a byproduct, making it a platform holding data. Structured product and order data is what agents need to shop on a merchant's behalf, which adds demand as agentic commerce grows. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading independent commerce platform.

News Corp owns Dow Jones, Factiva and The Wall Street Journal, making it a holder of proprietary news and business content that it licenses, including to AI developers. Proprietary content can be licensed to model builders. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and Dow Jones is a major business information brand.

The New York Times holds a large archive of proprietary journalism and licenses its databases and content, including to AI companies. Proprietary content can be licensed or built into products. Content is central but licensing is a smaller part, and it is a leading news publisher.

Pearson holds educational courseware, English language learning content and assessment data through Pearson VUE and its qualifications business, making it a holder of proprietary domain content. Domain content and assessment data are hard to replicate and can be licensed or built into AI learning and testing products. Content and assessments are a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading global education publisher and test provider.

Zillow runs real estate marketplaces that generate proprietary home listing, pricing and consumer data, making it a platform holding data. Real estate data supports AI valuation and search products. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading US real estate portal.

CarGurus runs auto marketplaces and sells data-driven market intelligence to dealers, making it a platform holding data. Vehicle pricing data supports AI products. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading US auto marketplace.

SS&C provides fund administration, investment accounting and healthcare software, holding financial and health data, making it vertical software holding data. Vertical data supports AI applications. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading fund administrator.

Broadridge processes proxy, investor communications and trade operations for financial firms, holding data on securities and investors, making it vertical software holding data. Vertical data supports AI products. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the dominant proxy processor.

Amadeus runs a global travel distribution network and the reservation, inventory and departure systems airlines and hotels operate on, holding booking and inventory data as a byproduct, making it vertical software and a network holding data. Travel network data is hard to replicate and supports AI for search, pricing and agent booking. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading global distribution system for travel.

Roper owns a portfolio of vertical software businesses in insurance, healthcare, government and other niches, making it a holder of vertical data. Vertical software data supports AI products. Vertical software is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a large consolidator of niche software.

HubSpot runs a CRM platform for mid-market businesses, holding customer and marketing data. CRM data supports agents for sales and service. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading SMB CRM.

Atlassian runs Jira and Confluence, holding enterprise knowledge and work data. Knowledge base and work data supports agents. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading collaboration platform.

Autodesk provides design and engineering software and the Vault data management solution, holding design data for AEC and manufacturing. Design data is domain-specific. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading design software vendor.

Bentley provides infrastructure engineering software, holding engineering and asset data. Domain data supports AI for infrastructure. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading infrastructure engineering vendor.
PTC provides CAD and PLM software with data management, holding product lifecycle data. Product data is domain-specific. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading PLM vendor.

Trimble provides construction, geospatial, agriculture and transportation software with data exchange and analytics, making it a vertical software company holding data. Domain data supports AI. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading construction technology vendor.

NetApp sells data management and storage software across hybrid clouds, positioning itself as data infrastructure for AI. Organizing enterprise data for AI adds demand. Data management is a meaningful part, and it is a leading enterprise storage vendor.

EXL provides data analytics, data governance and AI-driven operations for insurers, healthcare and other enterprises, making it a vendor that cleans, organizes and structures enterprise data. Most enterprise data is not agent ready, so data cleanup and governance work grows as companies deploy agents. Data analytics is central to its business, and it is a mid-sized analytics and operations firm.

Dropbox stores files for businesses and offers Dash, an AI search that retrieves content across a company's apps and files, making it a vendor that makes unstructured content usable. Unstructured content is much of what enterprises hold, and retrieval demand grows as agents need context. Content storage and retrieval is a meaningful part of the business, though it is a mature player with slow growth.

Progress provides data connectivity, application development and content tools, including DataDirect connectors. Making enterprise data usable adds demand. Data tools are a meaningful part of the business, and it is a mid-sized infrastructure software vendor.

UnitedHealth's Optum Insight sells software and data products to health systems, payers and life sciences, holding large healthcare data. Healthcare data is hard to replicate. Data is a meaningful but small part of the business, and Optum is a major health data holder.

GeneDx runs exome and genome sequencing and offers data and information services from its large rare disease genomic database. Genomic data is hard to replicate. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading rare disease testing lab.

Doximity runs a professional network used by most US physicians, holding proprietary data on clinicians and their activity. Platform data supports AI tools for physicians. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading US physician network.

Certara provides biosimulation software and clinical outcomes databases for drug development. Domain data supports AI models. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading biosimulation vendor.

Waystar runs healthcare payment and claims software, holding claims and payment data. Claims data supports AI for revenue cycle. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is a leading healthcare payments platform.

Baidu runs search and builds Ernie models on its data, making it a platform holding data. Search data supports models. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading Chinese search engine.

Recruit owns Indeed and Glassdoor, holding job, salary and employer data, making it a platform holding data. Labor market data is hard to replicate. Data is a meaningful part of the business, and it is the leading job marketplace.
